lines.say: In August twenty fifteen, a super typhoon hit Taipei, and something near the top of Taipei one-oh-one swung a full metre.
Wind makes a skyscraper sway, like a ruler flicked on a desk. Up top, people start to feel seasick.
So between floors eighty-seven and ninety-two, engineers hung a six-hundred-sixty-tonne steel ball.
It's a tuned mass damper. Its swing matches the tower's own rhythm,
so when wind shoves the tower one way, the heavy ball lags behind and pulls it back.
Eight hydraulic pistons soak up that motion and turn it into heat.
That cuts the sway by up to forty percent.
So in that typhoon, the ball moved a metre, so the people inside didn't have to.
Follow for how the world is really engineered.
